I am completely new to Python and I have installed the latest 2.X to my windows machine. I have added Python to my path, and I have chosen PyCharm as my IDE. Is there any thing I am missing or have overlooked that needs to be added or am I ready to get to programming ?

Edit: I should say that my programming background is in MATLAB and I want to do some similar programming in Python - math and science focused.
Look into using Python 3.x if at all possible. I understand that there are some limitations if libs that you need aren't in Python 3 yet, but if they are you should be using 3 for all new projects.

If you are looking something similar to matlab, you may want to start with a self contained package like anaconda or pythonXY or sage. I think pythonXY includes Spyder, which is a matlab like GUI as well.

These will include most of the libraries you will want to replicate matlab's capabilities (i.e., numpy, spicy, etc.).
iPython is also comparable to matlab.

Yes, and ipython is what I would recommend if you want something like the "shell mode" of matlab (which is probably what you use if you use matlab on linux).

I haven't used spyder recently, but I think it tries to replicate the gui version of matlab (ie, it includes thins like a variable viewer).

If you are doing math and science work, then you are in luck, python is great for that. Make sure you got scipy and numpy packages installed and get cracking. You should use Python 3, toss the textbook and help the language move forward.
